item.title: Why neutrinos matter as Francis Halzen wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics?
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-07
Why neutrinos matter as Francis Halzen wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics? The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics is announced in Stockholm, Sweden, Oct. 6, 2026. Francis Halzen has been awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics 2026 for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin, the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences announced Tuesday. (Xinhua/Lyu You) STOCKHOLM, Oct. 6 (Xinhua) -- Buried deep beneath the Antarctic ice, thousands of light sensors wait for flashes left by neutrinos, elusive particles that can travel across the universe almost undisturbed. By turning a cubic kilometre of South Pole ice into a giant detector, physicist Francis Halzen helped open a new window on the cosmos. The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded Halzen the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics on Tuesday "for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin." WHAT ARE NEUTRINOS, AND WHY DO THEY MATTER? Neutrinos are among the smallest known particles. They carry no electric charge, have extremely little mass, and interact so weakly with matter that most pass straight through the Earth without leaving a trace. Olle Eriksson, a member of the Nobel Committee for Physics and professor at Uppsala University, told Xinhua that detecting neutrinos is extremely challenging: "Through my thumbnail, there are 65 billion neutrinos that go through every second, and I don't feel it." But once detected, they can reveal information about events occurring far out in the universe. Scientists have long known that the cosmos contains natural particle accelerators capable of producing particles with energies far beyond those achievable in laboratories on Earth. The origins of the highest-energy cosmic particles, however, have remained difficult to trace. Cosmic rays carry electric charge and are deflected by magnetic fields as they travel through space. Neutrinos, unlike other particles, are electrically neutral and travel essentially in a straight line, allowing scientists to trace their direction back toward the violent environments where they were produced. This photo taken on Dec. 12, 2025 shows the Lemaire Channel in Antarctica. (Photo by Yang Shu/Xinhua) HOW DID HALZEN TURN SOUTH POLE ICE INTO A TELESCOPE? In 1988, Halzen, the Belgian-born scientist, presented the idea of installing light sensors deep in Antarctic ice. When one of the rare neutrinos collides with an atomic nucleus, it can produce a charged particle that generates a faint flash of blue light as it moves through the transparent ice. Sensors can capture that light and help scientists reconstruct where the neutrino came from. The idea eventually became IceCube, a detector using an entire cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice. Completed in 2011, it contains 5,160 light sensors, mostly between about 1,450 and 2,450 metres below the surface. The depth matters. "There, the ice is very clear, no air bubbles, no dirt, no dust," said Eriksson, adding that this condition allows faint flashes to travel hundreds of metres before being absorbed. The effort paid off. In 2013, IceCube researchers reported the first strong evidence for high-energy neutrinos arriving from distant space. With more data, they were able to establish that some of the particles originated far outside the solar system. Eriksson said the achievement helps humanity better understand its surroundings and its place in the universe by providing information about extreme cosmic events that cannot easily be obtained in other ways. The immediate significance lies mainly in expanding fundamental knowledge, he said, adding that major scientific discoveries can also lead to practical applications that were impossible to foresee when the research began. The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics is announced in Stockholm, Sweden, Oct. 6, 2026. Francis Halzen has been awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics 2026 for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin, the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences announced Tuesday. (Xinhua/Lyu You) WHY HALZEN, AND WHAT COMES NEXT? IceCube is the work of a large international collaboration involving hundreds of scientists and engineers. "Even though it is a large collaboration, we could still identify one person who was the pivotal, most important contributor to that experimental buildup and the experimental discovery," said Eriksson. "It was a long journey, but ... it finally worked," Halzen recalled the early phases at Tuesday's Nobel press conference, describing how the success was not guaranteed nearly 40 years ago but made possible by critical contributions from many people. The journey is continuing. Scientists are planning IceCube-Gen2, which is expected to expand the instrumented volume at the South Pole to about eight cubic kilometres, while other neutrino observatories are being developed around the world. Halzen said opening a new window on the universe often leads to unexpected discoveries. For neutrino astronomy, that window may only have begun to open. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: China firmly opposes U.S. arms sales to China's Taiwan region: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-07
China firmly opposes U.S. arms sales to China's Taiwan region: spokesperson BEIJING, Oct. 6 (Xinhua) -- China remains firmly opposed to U.S. arms sales to China's Taiwan region, Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Tuesday, stressing that the country's position is clear. Guo made the remarks in response to media reports that Taiwan recently received two F-16V fighter jets purchased from the United States and plans to receive another 64 within the year. Guo said the U.S. side needs to implement the important common understandings reached at the meeting between the two countries' presidents, abide by the one-China principle and the three China-U.S. joint communiques, and act prudently on the Taiwan question. "The Taiwan question is China's internal affair, and resolving it is a matter for the Chinese ourselves that brooks no external interference," he said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: China urges France, Germany to uphold open cooperation, free trade
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-07
China urges France, Germany to uphold open cooperation, free trade BEIJING, Oct. 6 (Xinhua) -- China hopes that France and Germany will uphold open cooperation and free trade, observe World Trade Organization rules, and refrain from encouraging the European Union (EU) to use protectionist tools at every turn, a spokesperson for the Ministry of Commerce said on Tuesday. When asked to comment on media reports that France and Germany had urged the EU to make greater use of trade defense measures and roll out a number of new protectionist tools, the spokesperson said China has always maintained that interdependence is not a risk, intertwined interests do not pose a threat, and open cooperation represents the right path to development. Protectionism cannot enhance competitiveness, and decoupling and cutting off supply chains will only harm others without benefiting oneself, the spokesperson said. As major economies, France and Germany should not politicize trade and economic issues or overstretch the concept of national security. They should avoid going down the wrong path in the wrong way, which would ultimately backfire on themselves, the spokesperson added. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Russian tourism industry eyes attracting more Chinese visitors
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-07
Russian tourism industry eyes attracting more Chinese visitors People visit the 12th Red Square Book Festival in Moscow, Russia, on June 4, 2026. (Xinhua/Feng Kaihua) MOSCOW, Oct. 7 (Xinhua) -- During China's week-long National Day holiday this year, Chinese tourists are frequently seen on the streets of Moscow. "Russia is a unique country and a must-visit," said Wang Xinzuo, who visited several Russian cities and described his trip as smooth and enjoyable. In the first half of 2026, Chinese tourists accounted for over 50 percent of all inbound tourist trips to Russia. "We are witnessing a substantial rise in travel volumes. In 2025, the number of mutual tourist visits exceeded 3 million. According to our data, 154,200 Chinese tourists visited Russia in the first quarter alone this year, marking a 44 percent increase year on year," Chinese Ambassador to Russia Zhang Hanhui said before the holiday. Russia is preparing for further growth. In early September, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Dmitry Chernyshenko said the country aims to accommodate more than 5.5 million Chinese tourists by 2030. Behind the figures lies an industry adapting to a new generation of Chinese travelers. MOSCOW: FROM GROUP TO INDEPENDENT TRAVEL Moscow remains the main gateway for Chinese tourists. According to the Border Service of the Russian Federation, 240,000 Chinese tourists visited Moscow in the first half of 2026, up 7 percent year on year. But the profile of visitors is changing. Guided group tours are becoming less dominant as younger and more independent Chinese travelers arrive. More than 80 percent of travelers from China come to Moscow independently, including for business, according to Bulat Nurmukhanov, deputy chairman of the Moscow Tourism Committee. In response, a China Friendly certification program is expanding in Moscow, covering services such as Chinese-language information, adapted menus and trained staff. The Cosmos Hotel Group told Xinhua that two of its four- and five-star hotels in Moscow have received the certification, with more properties planned to join the program. Moscow has also strengthened its promotion in China through Chinese-language tourism services, social media and cooperation with Chinese travel platforms, while highlighting its cultural heritage and modern attractions. Tourist boats travel on the Moskva River in Moscow, Russia, July 11, 2026. (Xinhua/Feng Kaihua) REGIONS SEEK NEW OPPORTUNITIES Beyond Moscow, Russian regions are increasingly competing for Chinese tourists. In St. Petersburg, the number of Chinese tourists has risen by nearly 60 percent since 2021, according to Nana Gvichiya, deputy chair of the city's Tourism Development Committee. Chinese visitors are showing a growing interest not only in historical sites but also in local cuisine and creative spaces. In the Altai region, the number of Chinese tourists increased 1.5 times in 2025 from the previous year, exceeding 6,000 for the first time, said Alexander Baryshnikov, head of the regional Department for Tourism and Resort Development. Although the region receives fewer Chinese visitors than Moscow and St. Petersburg partly because of a lack of direct flights, local businesses are improving services and developing China-friendly tourism products. Several hotels and resorts have received China Friendly certification, while tour operators have developed specialized routes and promoted them through international exhibitions and Chinese social media. In Russia's Far East, the Amur region has recorded a 60 percent increase in Chinese tourists since the introduction of the visa-free policy between China and Russia in 2025, Governor Vasily Orlov said. The region plans more than 200 joint events with China in 2026. A planned cross-border cable car linking Blagoveshchensk and Heihe is also expected to boost tourism. Once completed, the journey between the two countries will take just over two minutes, with an annual capacity of 2.5 million passengers. A tourist takes photos of lanterns in St. Petersburg, Russia, Feb. 15, 2026. (Photo by Irina Motina/Xinhua) ADAPTING SERVICES The rapid growth has also exposed gaps in Russia's tourism infrastructure. Experts and tourists cite language barriers, difficulties with digital payments and a shortage of qualified staff, particularly outside major tourist destinations. "Special attention should be paid to the training of professional guides for Chinese groups in Russia," said Anastasia Pavlova, an expert on cultural and tourism cooperation at the Russian State University for the Humanities. Ilya Umansky, president of the Russian Union of Tourism Industry, stressed the need for closer cooperation between the two sides in the tourism sector. "Today we find ourselves in a unique state of revival of our mutual tourist exchanges," Umansky said. "I am confident that we have a great future." Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: New professions show China's industrial, livelihood progress
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-06
New professions show China's industrial, livelihood progress BEIJING, Oct. 6 (Xinhua) -- A stream of new occupations is emerging at the forefront of China's new technologies, industries and business models, mirroring industrial upgrading and improvements in people's livelihoods. In the low-altitude economy sector alone, newly added positions such as drone swarm flight planners, low-altitude logistics specialists, and low-altitude intelligent connected system administrators stand out in the eighth batch of new professions recently released by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and other government departments. Occupations tied to the booming digital economy are also reshaping work in China, including AI engineering technicians, intelligent connected vehicle testers, embodied intelligent robot application technicians, and microgrid administrators, among others. The release of 11 new occupations and 23 new job types in the eighth batch marks a fresh update to the country's occupational catalog. Such updates serve as a talent "barometer" reflecting the pulse of China's industrial transformation, industry insiders noted. Take the low-altitude economy for example. The first batch of new occupations, released in 2019, introduced the drone pilots to meet the urgent demand for drone operations. The second batch added drone assembly and maintenance technicians, a role created to close the gap in equipment operation and maintenance for the emerging drone industry. As the drone industry has grown, new positions in the seventh and eighth batches have taken on responsibilities that expand from single technical operations to cross-cutting application fields such as logistics delivery, cultural tourism operations, and urban governance. The continuous release of new occupations reflects China's industrial system moving toward higher-end, smarter and greener development, said Li Qiang, vice president of online job-seeking platform Zhaopin. "Policy support expands and underpins the talent supply, while the job market absorbs in tandem. New occupations are both a precise mapping of the industrial development trends and a positive guide for the talent market," Li said. Beyond industrial upgrading, changes in China's new occupations also reflect evolving demands in people's livelihoods, with new jobs in the modern services sector continuing to expand. Industry insiders noted that as people's quality of life has been improving, producer services have moved toward specialization and the higher end of the value chain, while consumer services have developed toward higher quality, greater diversity, and convenience. The size of China's service sector is expected to expand beyond 100 trillion yuan (about 14.8 trillion U.S. dollars) in the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), according to the National Development and Reform Commission, the country's top economic planner. Industry insiders say the consumer services sector will be explored to unlock economic growth potential, with broad scope for developing residential services, health services, aged care, and childcare. Therefore, progress in this sector is expected to generate even more new jobs. China has been dynamically updating its occupational classification catalog. Since 2019, the country has issued eight batches of 121 new occupations. In 2020, the second batch introduced health-related new professions including healthcare attendants and rehabilitation assistive technology consultants. Subsequent batches continued this momentum, adding niche occupations and job types such as ski patrol rescuers, family education instructors, age-friendly renovation designers, and incense-making artisans. China's State Council has issued a plan to implement the employment-first strategy during the 15th Five-Year Plan period, calling for stronger synergy among macroeconomic policies on employment and highlighting efforts to stabilize employment in labor-intensive industries, expand employment in the service sector, and tap employment potential in emerging fields. "The emergence of new occupations is a direct response to new applications of technologies, fresh market changes, and new consumer demands," said Li Chang'an, a researcher at the Academy of China Open Economy Studies under the University of International Business and Economics. "Every update of the occupational catalog will inject more talent-driven momentum into the country's industrial development in the future alongside the advancement of the occupational standard system, alignment between talent cultivation and supply, and rules and systems to safeguard the progress of the sector," Li added. item.title: Longer trips, richer experiences: China's National Day holiday reveals shifting tourism trends
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-06
Longer trips, richer experiences: China's National Day holiday reveals shifting tourism trends * Chinese travelers have ventured farther during the National Day holiday, with family trips and experience-oriented travel on the rise. * Former revolutionary base areas have drawn renewed interest from holidaymakers, with visits offering travelers a chance to learn about the country's revolutionary history and reflect on the difficult years that helped shape modern China. * More international travelers are flocking to China to experience the country for themselves, riding a rising wave of global fascination with everything from the scenery and culture to its lifestyles and, more recently, Chinese brands and design. Tourists visit Guandu ancient town in Kunming, southwest China's Yunnan Province, Oct. 3, 2026. (Xinhua/Hu Chao) BEIJING, Oct. 5 (Xinhua) -- Five days into China's week-long National Day holiday, millions are still immersed in the sights, sounds and flavors of the season -- traveling, dining, exploring and enjoying the break. Yet this year, the scenes are subtly different. Travelers have ventured farther as the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday fell just three days before the National Day holiday, while family trips and experience-oriented travel are on the rise, according to travel agencies. "It points to a fundamental shift in the logic of tourism consumption, as travelers focus more on the quality of time and the richness of their experiences," said Bu Xiting, a researcher with the Communication University of China. LONGER BREAKS, RICHER CHOICES Data from Chinese online travel platform Tuniu shows that tours of 10 days or more are particularly popular during this holiday period, accounting for 26 percent of bookings. Yuan You, an internet company employee, spent three days of her 13-day break in Jiuzhaigou, southwest China's Sichuan Province, before heading to the provincial capital Chengdu for woodworking classes. "The holiday is rich while maintaining a relaxed pace," she said. Authorities across the country have rolled out a wide range of activities, consumer vouchers and subsidies to spur holiday spending. Shanghai, for example, has launched about 200 major consumption events, backed by consumer vouchers worth roughly 100 million yuan (around 14.85 million U.S. dollars). The offerings range from watching films and dining to purchasing digital products and cars, encouraging consumers to explore a broader spectrum of spending experiences. Cultural institutions, too, are broadening the ways people can experience and consume culture. The Sichuan Museum extended its holiday hours and launched a themed night tour, while Beijing's Zhongshan Park brought museums, cultural institutions and innovative brands together to create a market street featuring culture-inspired products. As more new energy vehicles hit the roads during the holiday, authorities have taken measures to ensure adequate charging facilities and convenient services. During last year's eight-day Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holiday period, Chinese travelers made 888 million domestic trips and spent a combined 809 billion yuan, according to the Ministry of Culture and Tourism. This year, data shows that foot traffic and revenue at 78 major shopping streets and commercial districts monitored by the Ministry of Commerce rose 3.4 percent and 5.3 percent year on year, respectively, from Oct. 1 to 3. Tourists visit the historical site of the Zunyi Meeting in Zunyi City, southwest China's Guizhou Province, Oct. 2, 2026. (Photo by Luo Xinghan/Xinhua) RED TOURISM, ROBOTS AND RURAL EXPERIENCES As China marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March, former revolutionary base areas have drawn renewed interest from holidaymakers, with visits offering travelers a chance to learn about the country's revolutionary history and reflect on the difficult years that helped shape modern China. In Yan'an, northwest China's Shaanxi Province, a street has staged special activities including performances of songs from the revolutionary years and a large-scale bonfire gathering. Visitor numbers on the first day of the holiday rose about 20 percent year on year. The holiday has also turned some of China's newest robots into part of the consumer experience, putting embodied intelligence to work alongside traditional culture in tourist attractions, shopping districts and ancient towns. At a cultural district in Chengdu, robots performed dances inspired by local opera's face-changing art and used digital technology to recreate tanghua, a traditional form of sugar painting. On Chunxi Road, a humanoid robot has gone beyond entertainment to take on the role of a store manager, greeting customers and recommending products rather than simply performing for them. China's growing network of robot training bases is preparing more machines for roles beyond the factory floor -- and beyond the country's borders. In the first half of 2026, Chinese manufacturers accounted for 97 percent of humanoid robot shipments worldwide, according to a report released at the 2026 World Robot Conference. Years of efforts to restore the environment and revitalize rural areas are also paying off. On a ridge overlooking the Miyun Reservoir in Beijing, visitors can hike to a viewing platform and enjoy outdoor concerts amid the pine trees. With roads, infrastructure and public services extending deeper into the countryside, some once-remote villages are emerging as new destinations for holidaymakers. Caijiagou, a former impoverished hillside village in east China's Shandong Province, has transformed into an art-themed destination, with murals adorning residential walls. Village official Liang Yunhui said the village has repurposed idle rural homes into cultural spaces such as an art gallery and a musical instrument museum, while hosting events featuring traditional crafts, cultural fairs and folk music. "In total, we have received more than 500,000 visits over the years," he said. On travel platform Fliggy, the number of users purchasing travel products featuring natural scenery and villages surged by nearly 50 percent from the same holiday period last year. "More travelers are seeking immersive experiences, from sampling local cuisine and making intangible cultural heritage crafts to watching distinctive performances, allowing them to gain a deeper appreciation of local culture," said a manager with Tuniu. Tourists from South Korea pose for a group photo at the Jiuzhaigou scenic spot in southwest China's Sichuan Province, Aug. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Wang Xi) CHINA HAUL While many Chinese tourists are venturing farther around the world, more international travelers are flocking to China to experience the country for themselves, riding a rising wave of global fascination with everything from the scenery and culture to its lifestyles and, more recently, Chinese brands and design. Tennis star Novak Djokovic, in Beijing for the China Open, was seen trying his hand at Chinese calligraphy at the Summer Palace, a former imperial garden. After a match, he used a traditional Chinese seal to put his mark on fans' keepsakes instead of signing autographs. Huaqiangbei, a sprawling electronics marketplace in south China's tech hub Shenzhen, has become a magnet for foreign shoppers looking to experience China's tech scene firsthand. Bryan Lamothe-Arice from the United States was browsing smart devices. "I'm particularly interested in the electric bikes and all kinds of flying devices here. I'm going to tell my friends to come here. There are tech products everywhere." China's border crossings are expected to see about 2.15 million passenger trips a day on average during the National Day holiday, according to the National Immigration Administration. That growing international interest is also showing up in spending. Overseas visitors spent 263.6 billion yuan in China in the first seven months of 2026, up 27.8 percent year on year, according to the commerce ministry. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: Holiday travel highlights China's transport strength, economic vitality
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-06
Holiday travel highlights China's transport strength, economic vitality Passengers prepare to board a train at Nanjing South Railway Station in Nanjing, east China's Jiangsu Province, Sept. 30, 2026. China's railway network saw a peak in passenger flow on Wednesday, one day before the beginning of the seven-day National Day holiday. (Photo by Su Yang/Xinhua) BEIJING, Oct. 5 (Xinhua) -- For Zhang Yang and his family in Ankang, northwest China's Shaanxi Province, this year's National Day holiday was a memorable one. On Oct. 1, following the opening of the Xi'an-Ankang high-speed railway, they took a direct high-speed train from Ankang to Yan'an, a city known for its revolutionary history. The journey, which used to take more than seven hours, now takes just over two hours. The Zhang family was among millions on the move during the National Day holiday from Oct. 1 to 7, one of China's peak periods for travel and spending. Data from the Ministry of Transport showed cross-regional passenger trips exceeded 300 million on each of the first three days of the holiday. China State Railway Group Co., Ltd. (China Railway) said the country's railways handled over 25.2 million passenger trips on Oct. 1, setting a new single-day record. For a country as vast as China, moving hundreds of millions of people during a holiday rush is a feat of scale. Behind this feat lies a transport network built up over decades. By the end of 2025, China's comprehensive transport network spanned more than 6 million km, including the world's largest high-speed rail network. High-speed railways, expressways, airports and ports connect cities, towns and rural areas across the country. The network is continuing to expand. On Sept. 28, China opened four major high-speed railway sections across northern, northwestern, central and northeastern China, with a combined length of more than 1,100 km. The new lines further shorten travel times and put more destinations within easy reach of families like Zhang's. China's transport development goes beyond faster journeys. Better supporting services are also making travel more convenient. New energy vehicles (NEVs) have become increasingly common among Chinese households and are now a popular choice for long-distance travel. The Ministry of Transport expects NEV trips on expressways during the holiday to reach 1.8 times the usual level, pushing up demand for charging services. China's extensive charging infrastructure is helping to meet growing demand. The country now has more than 24 million EV charging facilities, forming the world's largest EV charging network. Highway service areas have about 89,000 charging facilities in total, covering virtually all service areas. To handle the holiday peak, mobile emergency chargers have been added at key service areas, while drivers are encouraged to leave after charging their batteries to 80 percent to improve charging turnover. Faster connections and more convenient services are making it easier for travelers to visit more destinations in a single trip. Data from online travel platform Qunar showed that nearly 30 percent of travelers had booked hotels in at least two cities, while bookings involving stays in four or more cities surged 53 percent year on year. The trend extends beyond China's borders. China's expanding transport links are supporting a rise in cross-border travel, with Chinese airlines operating regular international passenger routes connecting 177 cities in 80 countries. For outbound travel, Qunar data showed that hotel bookings for multi-country trips more than doubled year on year during the holiday. Inbound tourism also recorded double-digit growth, according to Trip.com Group, with day-tour bookings up more than fourfold and train ticket bookings up more than 170 percent year on year during the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day breaks. The transport network that carries millions of travelers is also keeping goods moving, linking businesses and markets and sustaining economic activity across the country. Even during the holiday, the Liujing operating area of Nanning Port in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region bustles with activity, as ship horns sound and workers load and unload goods. The increase in cargo traffic is closely linked to the opening of the Pinglu Canal. Stretching 134.2 km from Hengzhou in Guangxi to the Beibu Gulf, the canal opened to navigation on Sept. 16, providing a shorter river-sea route for cargo from southwest China to international markets. Bulk cargo, including construction materials, auto parts and grain, is being shipped from Nanning Port via the Pinglu Canal to the Beibu Gulf for export. On average, the route now handles an additional 20,000 tonnes of cargo per day. "We expect to transport 200,000 tonnes of cargo during the National Day holiday," said You Tong, deputy manager of the production operations center at Nanning Port Development and Investment Co., Ltd. You said the port has optimized operations and maintained round-the-clock staffing to keep cargo moving smoothly during the holiday surge. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online.
